title: Initialize a repository
requirement: The CLI shall initialize a repository-local Roadmap workspace with the files and directories needed to begin planning work.
acceptance_criteria: From a valid repository, initialization creates a usable workspace; invalid input returns actionable guidance; no partial workspace remains after failure.

title: Manage issues
requirement: The CLI shall support the complete issue lifecycle from capture through archival while preserving identity and history.
acceptance_criteria: A user can create, find, inspect, prioritize, assign, update, progress, close, archive, and restore an issue; every successful step is visible in a subsequent read.

title: Plan with projects and milestones
requirement: The CLI shall organize work into projects and milestones that communicate scope, sequence, due dates, and progress.
acceptance_criteria: A maintainer can establish a project and milestone, assign issues, inspect scope and progress, and close or archive completed planning artifacts without losing traceability.

title: See and advance current priorities
requirement: The CLI shall help a developer select the most relevant work and advance it through a visible workflow.
acceptance_criteria: The daily view identifies current, overdue, and high-priority work; the developer can start, update, block, review, and complete an item without losing context.

title: Work offline with portable data
requirement: Users shall be able to read and manage core project data without a network connection or proprietary service.
acceptance_criteria: Core issue, milestone, project, requirement, configuration, and reporting operations work without network access; canonical data remains human-readable and version-controllable.

title: Automate status from Git activity
requirement: The CLI shall connect Roadmap work to branches and recognized commit activity through explicit, reversible Git integration.
acceptance_criteria: A user can set up integration, link work to a branch, apply a documented commit transition, inspect status, and remove automation without corrupting project data or unrelated hooks.

title: Synchronize with an optional remote
requirement: Users shall be able to synchronize supported Roadmap entities with GitHub or Git while retaining a usable local source of truth.
acceptance_criteria: A configured user can preview, baseline, pull, reconcile, push, recover, and audit a sync; conflicts remain explicit and local-only operation remains available.

title: Use human and machine-readable output
requirement: The CLI shall expose stable human-readable and machine-readable output suitable for terminals, scripts, exports, and stakeholder reports.
acceptance_criteria: Supported commands produce documented rich, plain, JSON, CSV, or Markdown output; machine-readable stdout parses cleanly and contains no presentation noise.

title: Protect credentials and sensitive data
requirement: The CLI shall keep credentials and sensitive values out of repository data, command output, and routine logs.
acceptance_criteria: Credentials use an approved system credential facility; output and logs are redacted; missing or inaccessible credentials produce remediation guidance without revealing values.

title: Diagnose project health
requirement: The CLI shall identify invalid configuration, malformed entities, broken links, naming problems, dependency faults, and storage inconsistencies.
acceptance_criteria: Health results identify the affected entity, severity, evidence, and corrective action and offer stable exit codes or structured output for automation.

title: Recover from destructive changes
requirement: The CLI shall provide confirmation, dry-run, backup, archive, restore, checkpoint, or rollback safeguards appropriate to destructive operations.
acceptance_criteria: A maintainer can preview risk, cancel safely, recover supported entities after interruption or error, and verify that identity and relationships remain intact.

title: Understand and act on failures
requirement: The CLI shall return concise, actionable errors and a non-success exit status when an operation cannot be completed.
acceptance_criteria: Validation, filesystem, Git, credential, network, conflict, and data-integrity failures identify what failed, what changed, and the safest next action without an unhandled traceback in normal mode.

title: Install and verify the CLI
requirement: A supported user shall be able to install the published package and invoke help and version commands without repository-specific environment workarounds.
acceptance_criteria: A clean supported environment installs the release artifact; `roadmap --help` and `roadmap --version` exit successfully; the reported version matches package metadata.

title: Preview initialization
requirement: A user shall be able to preview initialization choices and filesystem changes before modifying a repository.
acceptance_criteria: Dry-run reports the intended directory, project, template, integration, and overwrite actions; it creates or changes no project files.

title: Open or safely reinitialize a workspace
requirement: The CLI shall detect an existing workspace and either open it unchanged or require explicit intent before reinitialization or overwrite.
acceptance_criteria: Normal invocation preserves existing data; force or migration paths display impact, create recovery evidence, and produce a valid workspace or restore the prior state.

title: Inspect and change configuration
requirement: A maintainer shall be able to view, get, set, validate, and reset supported configuration values.
acceptance_criteria: Valid changes persist and are reflected by subsequent commands; invalid keys or values are rejected; reset states its scope and preserves secrets unless explicitly included.

title: Create a complete issue
requirement: A contributor shall be able to capture a work item with title, description, type, priority, assignee, milestone, labels, estimate, and relationships as applicable.
acceptance_criteria: The issue receives a stable ID and timestamps; supplied fields round-trip; invalid references are rejected; omitted optional fields receive documented defaults.

title: Find and inspect issues
requirement: Users shall be able to list, filter, search, sort, select columns, and view details for active, backlog, blocked, overdue, assigned, and archived work.
acceptance_criteria: Queries return only matching issues in deterministic order; empty results are explicit; detail views include relationships and remote identifiers when requested.

title: Prioritize, assign, and organize an issue
requirement: A maintainer shall be able to update issue metadata, assign ownership, and move work between backlog and milestones with a recorded reason.
acceptance_criteria: The intended issue changes once; invalid assignees or milestones are rejected; related milestone and project views reconcile after the change.

title: Manage workflow state and progress
requirement: A developer shall be able to start, progress, block, unblock, move to review, and close an assigned issue using valid state transitions.
acceptance_criteria: Each transition updates status, progress, timestamps, and reason consistently; invalid transitions fail without mutation; closed work appears in completion views.

title: Manage dependencies and critical path
requirement: Users shall be able to add, remove, replace, inspect, and analyze issue dependencies without creating invalid graphs.
acceptance_criteria: Missing targets, self-links, duplicates, and prohibited cycles are rejected; blocking state is visible; critical-path output explains the calculated sequence.

title: Discuss work in context
requirement: Users shall be able to create, list, edit, and delete comments attached to issues or milestones.
acceptance_criteria: Comments retain stable identity, author, target, and timestamps; edits and deletions affect only the selected comment; malformed comment data is diagnosed.

title: Preserve implementation context
requirement: A developer shall be able to connect an issue to its branch, remote issue, implementation work, and verification evidence so another contributor can resume it.
acceptance_criteria: The issue detail view exposes valid links; broken or duplicate links are diagnosed; unlinking removes only the selected relation and preserves the issue.

title: Review a daily work summary
requirement: A developer shall be able to see assigned in-progress, overdue, high-priority, and recently completed work for the upcoming milestone.
acceptance_criteria: The summary uses the configured identity and next milestone, avoids unrelated work, explains empty states, and offers a verbose view when needed.

title: Create and maintain a project
requirement: A maintainer shall be able to create, inspect, update, close, archive, restore, and delete a top-level project.
acceptance_criteria: Project identity and repository metadata persist; destructive actions require appropriate confirmation; linked milestones remain traceable through close, archive, and restore.

title: Create and maintain a milestone
requirement: A maintainer shall be able to create, inspect, update, and assign a consistently named milestone with description, due date, and optional project.
acceptance_criteria: Naming and dates validate; the milestone has stable identity; assignment is visible from both issue and milestone views.

title: Review milestone scope and progress
requirement: Users shall be able to inspect milestone scope in list, detail, board, and recalculated progress views.
acceptance_criteria: Counts and progress derive from current linked issues; board columns reflect workflow state; empty and overdue milestones are explicit.

title: Close and retain delivery history
requirement: A maintainer shall be able to close, archive, restore, or delete projects and milestones with clear effects on linked work.
acceptance_criteria: Close preserves history; archive moves the intended artifact; restore returns it without duplication; delete requires explicit confirmation and handles linked entities according to policy.

title: Configure and inspect Git integration
requirement: A developer shall be able to configure repository integration and inspect repository, authentication, hook, branch, and work-link status.
acceptance_criteria: Setup detects supported repository context; status distinguishes configured, degraded, and unavailable components and gives a safe next action.

title: Manage Git hooks reversibly
requirement: A developer shall be able to preview, install, configure, inspect, and uninstall Roadmap Git hooks without overwriting unrelated hook behavior.
acceptance_criteria: Repeated install is idempotent; existing hooks are preserved or composed; status reports exact installation state; uninstall removes only Roadmap-managed content.

title: Update work from commit messages
requirement: Recognized commit references shall apply only documented issue transitions and shall ignore unrelated text.
acceptance_criteria: Valid references identify one issue and transition; malformed, ambiguous, or unknown references report or safely skip; repeated processing is idempotent.

title: Create and link an issue branch
requirement: A developer shall be able to create a valid branch for an issue, optionally check it out, and link an existing current branch.
acceptance_criteria: Dirty-tree and branch-collision risks are reported; generated names are safe; force behavior is explicit; subsequent status and issue views show the link.

title: Configure remote authentication and scope
requirement: A user shall be able to select a Git or GitHub backend, detect or specify repository scope, store credentials safely, and validate access.
acceptance_criteria: Valid configuration identifies the backend and repository; credentials are not persisted in project files; invalid scope or access fails before data mutation.

title: Establish and preview a sync baseline
requirement: A user shall be able to choose an initial local, remote, or interactive baseline and preview the resulting sync plan without applying it.
acceptance_criteria: Dry-run lists creates, updates, deletes, links, duplicates, and conflicts; baseline choice is explicit; preview changes no local or remote entity.

title: Push, pull, or synchronize selected work
requirement: A user shall be able to push, pull, or two-way sync supported entities with optional milestone, state, and date filters.
acceptance_criteria: Only selected entities transfer; mappings preserve supported fields and links; repeated sync is idempotent; a summary reports applied and skipped work.

title: Resolve synchronization conflicts
requirement: The CLI shall surface three-way conflicts and allow explicit local, remote, or interactive resolution without silently discarding critical-field changes.
acceptance_criteria: Conflict views show baseline, local, and remote values; the selected resolution is applied once and recorded; cancellation leaves recoverable state.

title: Resume or safely retry failed synchronization
requirement: A user shall be able to understand partial sync failure and resume or retry from a checkpoint without duplicating completed changes.
acceptance_criteria: Failure reports the last durable checkpoint and local/remote effects; resume is idempotent; unrecoverable cases provide manual recovery instructions.

title: Manage duplicates and remote links
requirement: A user shall be able to detect, review, resolve, link, unlink, and validate duplicate or mismatched local-to-remote entities.
acceptance_criteria: Dry-run shows proposed matching and deletion; thresholds and decisions are explicit; no valid local entity is deleted solely from an uncertain fuzzy match.

title: Inspect synchronization status and metrics
requirement: Users shall be able to inspect link status, recent sync activity, conflicts, errors, duration, and outcome metrics.
acceptance_criteria: Views distinguish current state from historical metrics, redact sensitive values, support structured output where documented, and explain when no history exists.

title: Choose stable output formats
requirement: Users shall be able to request supported output formats and columns without changing command meaning.
acceptance_criteria: Rich and plain views remain readable; JSON and CSV parse; Markdown is valid; exit status and stderr behavior remain stable across formats.

title: Export filtered data and reports
requirement: A user shall be able to export selected Roadmap data and generate summary, detailed, or analytics reports to an explicit destination.
acceptance_criteria: The file format and schema are documented; filters match interactive queries; overwrite behavior is explicit; empty exports remain valid.

title: Run actionable health scans
requirement: A maintainer shall be able to scan selected entity types and severities, include dependency checks, group results, and consume stable exit codes.
acceptance_criteria: Healthy, degraded, and unhealthy results map to documented exit codes; each finding identifies entity, rule, severity, and remediation; JSON and CSV parse.

title: Preview and apply targeted health fixes
requirement: A maintainer shall be able to preview and selectively apply safe fixes with confirmation and a post-fix report.
acceptance_criteria: Dry-run is non-mutating; only selected fix types run; every mutation is reported and recoverable; a follow-up scan verifies the result.

title: Clean backups and malformed data safely
requirement: A maintainer shall be able to inspect and clean old backups, misplaced files, duplicates, and malformed entities without broad unintended deletion.
acceptance_criteria: Targeted and all-mode previews enumerate exact paths and actions; retention rules are honored; failures are surfaced; recoverable data is preserved.

title: Validate database and remote-link integrity
requirement: A maintainer shall be able to compare canonical files with local indexes and remote-link state and preview repair or pruning.
acceptance_criteria: Missing, extra, duplicate, or mismatched records are reported; auto-fix and prune affect only confirmed inconsistencies; canonical data remains readable.

title: Edit and move canonical data
requirement: Users shall be able to inspect or edit supported canonical files with ordinary tools and move a workspace across supported systems.
acceptance_criteria: Valid manual edits are loaded on the next command; invalid edits produce diagnostics; path, newline, and encoding differences do not change entity meaning.

title: Restore data after an interrupted or destructive operation
requirement: A maintainer shall be able to identify the relevant backup, archive, or checkpoint and restore the selected scope without creating duplicates.
acceptance_criteria: Restore can be previewed; restored entities retain stable IDs and relationships; the operation reports overwritten or skipped data and supports post-restore validation.

title: Upgrade and migrate a workspace
requirement: A user shall be able to upgrade the CLI and migrate supported workspace data with compatibility checks, preview, backup, and rollback guidance.
acceptance_criteria: The CLI detects schema/version differences; migration is idempotent; unsupported downgrade or breaking changes stop before mutation and link to a migration path.

title: Create a requirement artifact
requirement: A user shall be able to create a user or technical requirement with a stable ID, statement, rationale, priority, owner, lifecycle status, and acceptance or verification evidence.
acceptance_criteria: The requirement is stored in the canonical file-first format; type-specific required fields validate; defaults are explicit; duplicate IDs are rejected.

title: Find and inspect requirements
requirement: Users shall be able to list, filter, search, sort, and view requirements by type, journey, stage, priority, status, owner, relation, and roadmap target.
acceptance_criteria: Results are deterministic; detail shows statement, evidence, history, and typed relations; missing or superseded IDs produce clear guidance.

title: Review and transition requirement status
requirement: Authorized project participants shall be able to propose edits and explicitly transition requirements through Draft, Accepted, In Progress, Verified, Deferred, Rejected, or superseded states.
acceptance_criteria: Invalid transitions and unauthorized assumptions are rejected; accepted meaning changes remain reviewable; status reasons and timestamps are retained.

title: Link requirements to intent, work, and evidence
persona: Product owner, architect, developer, or reviewer
requirement: Users shall be able to create and inspect typed relationships among user requirements, technical requirements, issues, milestones, projects, external work, tests, and evidence.
acceptance_criteria: Missing or invalid targets and prohibited cycles are rejected; links are visible from both relevant views; unlinking preserves both artifacts.

title: Measure traceability and coverage
requirement: Users shall be able to find accepted requirements without planned work, completed work without verification, orphan work, broken relations, and coverage by journey, priority, milestone, or release.
acceptance_criteria: Coverage definitions are visible; counts reconcile to underlying artifacts; gaps link to affected IDs; Roadmap does not fabricate or auto-approve relationships.

title: Record acceptance evidence
requirement: A requirement owner shall be able to record verification evidence and mark a requirement Verified only when its stated criteria are satisfied.
acceptance_criteria: Evidence identifies type, location, result, reviewer, and date; missing evidence prevents verification; failed or stale evidence can reopen review without deleting history.

title: Import and export requirements
requirement: Users shall be able to export requirements to CSV and import reviewed CSV changes through a dry-run and conflict-aware transaction.
acceptance_criteria: Round-trip preserves supported fields and relations; preview reports creates, updates, invalid rows, and conflicts; failed import leaves canonical files unchanged.

title: Supersede or archive requirements without losing history
requirement: Users shall be able to supersede or archive obsolete requirements while keeping stable references, rationale, relations, and replacement links.
acceptance_criteria: The prior ID remains resolvable and immutable except for status/history metadata; replacement relationships are validated; reports exclude or include historical artifacts explicitly.

title: Build roadmap scope from accepted requirements
requirement: Users shall be able to select Accepted requirements into projects, milestones, or roadmap targets and monitor delivery and verification without conflating requirements with issues.
acceptance_criteria: Only eligible requirements are committed; implementation work remains distinct and linked; scope changes preserve decision history; progress distinguishes planned, implemented, and verified.

title: Configure and safely evolve a workspace
requirement: The CLI shall support configuration and version evolution without exposing secrets, silently changing meaning, or making supported workspace data unreadable.
acceptance_criteria: A maintainer can inspect and change configuration, upgrade the CLI, preview required migration, recover from failure, and reopen the workspace with equivalent supported data.

title: Manage intent through delivery and verification
persona: Product owner, architect, maintainer, or contributor
requirement: Roadmap shall support an optional end-to-end requirements-as-code journey from capture and governance through planning, implementation traceability, evidence, and supersession.
acceptance_criteria: A team can create and approve requirements, link distinct delivery work, identify coverage gaps, record verification evidence, and preserve history using repository-native artifacts.
